title: Geometric component count is locally constant in a proper smooth family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper smooth morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $s\in S$, let $n(s)$ be the number of connected components of $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$, where $\overline{\kappa(s)}$ is an algebraic closure of the residue field [def-weil-geometric-fibre] [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $n(s)$ is finite and $n:S\to\mathbf N$ is locally constant, including $n(s)=0$ for empty fibres. In particular, if $X_s$ is geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], there is an open neighbourhood of $s$ on which every fibre is geometrically connected.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, specialized to smooth morphisms (smooth implies flat with geometrically reduced fibres)

proof.text: Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The geometric fibre is the pullback along the algebraic-closure geometric point [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Its projection to the algebraic-closure spectrum is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and smooth by the same base-change stability. A smooth scheme over a field is reduced, using the existing isReduced_of_smooth theorem underlying [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced].

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, hypotheses; smooth specialization uses Tags 01VF and 056T

proof.text: The structure sheaf is invertible, hence of finite presentation, and is flat over the base of a flat morphism. Apply [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change], clause (2), in degree zero to obtain upper semicontinuity of its hFiber. The Lean API is isFlatOver_of_isInvertible followed by upperSemicontinuous_hFiber. The finiteness clause need not be applied separately.

source.place: Tag 0BDN, label lemma-jump-loci-geometric, finiteness of fibre cohomology and upper semicontinuity (source clause (2)), applied to the structure sheaf

proof.text: Use hFiber_pullback_of_isPullback, the already proved fibre-dimension consequence of [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom], on the geometric-point pullback square. The point of Spec of the algebraic closure maps to the chosen base point, and hFiber_eq_finrankH identifies the fibre dimension over this field with its cohomology dimension. Pullback preserves the unit structure sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] to the proper reduced geometric fibre. Compose its scalar-compatible ring equivalence with H.zeroLinearEquiv to obtain an algebraic-closure-linear equivalence from functions on the finite connected-component set to zeroth cohomology. Compatibility is checked by writing scalar multiplication as multiplication by the constant function, using the product theorem scalar-map clause. Taking finranks gives hFiber equal to Nat.card of connected components, including the empty scheme. Properness supplies the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness hypotheses of the base-change result by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, identification of component count with zeroth cohomology dimension; Tag 0BUG and flat base change

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-proper-component-count-lower-semicontinuous], using smooth-implies-flat and local finite presentation. Retain its function n, its equality with Nat.card, finiteness, the empty-fibre clause, and the lower-bound neighbourhoods.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, first sentence, invoking Tag 0BUI

proof.text: Identify n with hFiber by Step 3. At s, the upper-semicontinuity open set n(t) < n(s)+1 intersects the lower-bound neighbourhood from Step 4. On the intersection, Nat.le_antisymm gives n(t)=n(s), which proves IsLocallyConstant through iff_exists_open. Transfer this along the equality of n and Nat.card. Finiteness and the zero assertion are exactly the corresponding clauses retained from Step 4.

source.place: Tag 0E0N, label lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, final sentence: lower and upper semicontinuity imply local constancy

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] on the residue fibre, and the canonical pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso, to equate geometric connectedness of the residue fibre with connectedness of the geometric fibre. For any topological space, connectedness is equivalent to Nat.card of its connected components being one: forward the quotient is nonempty and subsingleton; reverse Nat.card_eq_one_iff_unique supplies a nonempty subsingleton quotient, so every point belongs to the component of a chosen point. Hence the fibre condition is n(t)=1. For a geometrically connected fibre at s, take the open fibre n(t)=n(s) of the locally constant function n. Every t in it satisfies n(t)=1 and is geometrically connected.
